title: 0. Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix

epigraph.quote: Separate the quality of the enterprise from the excitement of the chart—then buy only when both the cash flows and the price asymmetry stand on your side.
epigraph.author: Research Desk Underwriting Charter

web_blocks.html: What ABM Industries Does: Founded in 1909, ABM Industries Incorporated (NYSE: ABM) is a $9.15 billion (TTM) US integrated facility-services operator [1, 42]. The firm employs roughly 113,000 people across five core operating segments [1, 10, 11]. These units include Business & Industry (B&I, 47.2% of FY25 sales) and Manufacturing & Distribution (M&D, 18.5%) [1, 10]. Remaining divisions comprise Aviation (12.8%), Education (10.5%), and Technical Solutions (ATS, 11.0%) [1, 11]. Within ATS, ABM provides microgrids via RavenVolt, critical power via Quality Uptime, and EV/HVAC engineering [1, 11, 42]. Legacy janitorial and engineering contracts deliver steady recurring revenue across multi-year cycles [4, 42]. ABM also maintains a 58-year dividend-increase streak paying $1.16/sh at a 2.12% dividend yield [4, 42]. However, $2.59 billion of M&A goodwill depresses consolidated ROIC to 4.62% [4, 42]. This return trails ~8.5% WACC alongside a slender 1.82% GAAP net margin [4, 42]. Our price-blind fundamental audit therefore rates ABM as CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL with PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health.

Dual Verdict & Positioning (As of Nov 16, 2026 Close — $54.64): On the tape, ABM trades in a confirmed Stage 2 uptrend [42]. Shares have gained +40.5% over the past 6 months with a tight 5.95% Bollinger Band VCP squeeze [42]. The stock sits just 1.9% below its recent 52-week high of $55.70 [42]. However, weekly RSI of 71.89 signals stretched momentum while the broader US market experiences a Correction with 6 distribution days. Buying at $54.64 offers only 1.23:1 reward-to-risk toward our $64.00 Base Case against a $47.00 structural stop. Waiting for a pullback into the $51.36–$53.50 support shelf (10W EMA / 20D SMA) improves Base Case asymmetry to 1.62:1. This entry zone offers +19.6% upside versus -12.1% downside risk. Accordingly, our New Capital Verdict is WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (TIER_2). Our Current Holding Action is NOT_HELD (0 shares). Our Options Verdict is NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID, restricting positioning to common equity only. Marginal capital remains 100% in CASH pending an orderly pullback to support.

web_blocks.html: Monograph Roadmap & Capital Discipline: Chapters 1–6 establish ABM's operational reality strictly blind to stock price. Our analysis traces its century-long evolution and details all five revenue segments with concrete customer walkthroughs. We then trace the FY2025 $100 revenue-to-FCF waterfall and benchmark ABM's competitive moat against global peers. These chapters also audit CEO Scott Salmirs's ELEVATE transformation track record and examine 10-year balance-sheet forensics. Chapters 7–9 open the November 16, 2026 market tape at the closing price of $54.64. We deconstruct the Reverse DCF and evaluate peer valuation multiples against EMCOR, Comfort Systems, Aramark, Cintas, and Vestis. Finally, we audit the Stage 2 VCP chart pattern and inspect the illiquid options chain. These technical and valuation tests lock in our disciplined WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT ($51.36–$53.50) execution plan.

book_paragraphs: Welcome to our institutional monograph on ABM Industries Incorporated. Before we dive into the century-old story of how a San Francisco window-washing business grew into a $9.15 billion facility-services giant, let's put our independent conclusion right up front so you know exactly where the evidence leads.

We evaluated ABM in two strict, isolated stages. First, we locked the stock price in a drawer and audited the business purely on its operations, customer contracts, management track record, and 10-year cash flows. That blind audit earned a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL grade: ABM has genuine momentum in high-tech niches like RavenVolt microgrids and WGNSTAR semiconductor cleanrooms, alongside a 58-year dividend-increase streak, but $2.59 billion of acquisition goodwill keeps consolidated ROIC at 4.62%—below its cost of capital—on a razor-thin 1.82% net margin.

Second, we opened the November 16, 2026 market tape. At $54.64, ABM sits in a confirmed Stage 2 uptrend just 1.9% below its 52-week high of $55.70, trading at 12.59x forward earnings and 9.19x EV/EBITDA. While those headline multiples look reasonable, chasing a 40% six-month rally with weekly RSI at 71.89 during a market Correction gives us only 1.23:1 reward-to-risk to our $64.00 Base Case against a $47.00 structural stop.

Our New Capital Verdict is therefore WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT: let the market come to our $51.36–$53.50 buy zone along the 10-week EMA and 50-day SMA, where Base Case asymmetry improves to 1.62:1. With zero shares currently held in our portfolio (NOT_HELD) and listed options too illiquid to trade, we keep 100% of our marginal cash tranche in T-Bills today and let patience do the heavy lifting.

Over the next nine chapters, you and I will walk through ABM's business from the ground up. We'll visit semiconductor cleanrooms in the Pacific Northwest, airport terminals running automated baggage-handling maintenance, and commercial office towers where ABM engineers manage HVAC chillers and RavenVolt microgrids. We'll also put management's ELEVATE transformation promises under an unforgiving five-year microscope.

By the end of this monograph, you will know not only why ABM's stock has rallied 40.5% in six months, but also why its 4.62% ROIC keeps a strict ceiling on what we are willing to pay—and the exact price levels where risk and reward finally tilt in our favor.

A quick word on how to read this companion alongside the Web Research Desk dossier. Every single financial figure, segment percentage, moving average, support level, and scenario target in these pages matches the web tables 100%. The difference is perspective: while the web edition gives you dense institutional matrices and interactive charts for rapid verification, this narrative edition sits across the desk from you to explain why each number matters in the real world.

Keep three numbers in your pocket as we begin: 4.62% ROIC (why we refuse to overpay for ABM as a long-term compounder), $51.36–$53.50 (the Stage 2 pullback shelf where our reward-to-risk ratio clears 1.62:1), and $47.00 (the structural invalidation stop beneath the 30-week moving average). Everything else in these ten chapters builds the evidence around those three anchors.

As you turn to Chapter 1, keep an open mind and a sharp pencil. We are neither cheering for management's ELEVATE transformation nor dismissing a 117-year-old American industrial franchise out of hand. We are simply demanding that the numbers, the cash conversion, and the entry price all line up before a single dollar leaves our cash reserve.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Good investing is the art of matching price to business quality. ABM is a solid turnaround and FCF-normalization story, not a chase-at-all-costs compounder—so $51.36–$53.50 is our line in the sand.
